name: Central African Republic
headline: Central African Republic: +5.8% growth in 2025, 1.0% inflation, debt 43% of GDP
sections: Central African Republic is a $4.6 billion economy (2025), the world's 176th-largest of 215 measured. Real output grew +5.8% in 2025, faster than the world median of +3.5%. Income per person is $1,314 at purchasing-power parity (2025), against a world median of $21K. Manufacturing accounts for 18.0% of GDP (2023).

Consumer prices rose 1.0% in 2025, broadly within typical target ranges, down from 5.6% in 2022. Unemployment stood at 6.3% (2025), above the world median of 5.1%. Youth unemployment was 10.1% (2025).
Gross government debt is 43% of GDP (2025), a moderate level that has risen from 30% in 2020. The general government balance is −3.8% of GDP (2025), a deficit beyond the common 3% benchmark.
The current account balance is −2.6% of GDP (2025). Trade equals 53% of GDP (2025), a fairly open economy. Net FDI inflows were 1.4% of GDP (2025).
IMF projections put government debt at 48% of GDP by 2031, still rising from today's level. Life expectancy is 57.7 years (2024). Population: 5.5 million (2025).
note: Built from official World Bank and IMF data; IMF projections are labelled as projections.
